title: Label sampling strata cribnotes
content:
Purpose:
A compact personal reference for constructing sampling strata for labeling runs focused on long-tail labels and edge-case cleanup. This is intended for quick iteration when we need to generate micro-batches for human review or for small-scale evaluation sets.

Quick summary / guiding principles:
- Aim for clear stratification, not perfect probability matching. We want buckets that expose different failure modes to labelers and to the eval pipeline.
- Oversample rare but high-impact classes and near-boundary examples (confusions).
- Keep a small held-out random sample for calibration checks (5–10% of batch).
- Prefer reproducible deterministic filters (hash-based) for repeatability across runs.

Strata definitions (working):
1) frequent-clean: high-frequency label, low heuristic score noise. Use for sanity-check QA.
2) frequent-edge: high-frequency label but with heuristic signals for edge (e.g., punctuation anomalies, truncated text).
3) rare-high-impact: rare labels with product impact (e.g., security & compliance tags).
4) near-confusion: examples close to decision boundary between two labels (score delta < 0.08).
5) duplication-probe: high-similarity clusters (cosine>0.92) where one item gets different labels in history.
6) metadata-outlier: normal text but unusual metadata (unusual locale, empty user fields, extremely long context).
7) random-holdout: uniform random subsample for baseline metrics.

Heuristic rules for bucket assignment:
- Compute a primary label score and a second-best score; if (best - second) < 0.08 => near-confusion.
- Use tokenizer token count > 400 => mark metadata-outlier.
- If last_30d_label_frequency < 0.005 => candidate for rare-high-impact.
- Similarity dedupe: approximate nearest neighbors (FAISS / annoy). For dedupe-probe, sample clusters where label entropy > 0.3.
- Deterministic sampling: use sha1(id + run_seed) mod N for per-bucket quotas so re-runs yield identical sets if seed unchanged.

Batch composition suggestion (for 500-example run):
- 150 rare-high-impact
- 120 near-confusion
- 80 duplication-probe
- 50 frequent-edge
- 80 frequent-clean
- 20 metadata-outlier
- 0-10 reserved for manual curator picks
- 40 random-holdout

Labeler guidance snippets (to include in UI microcopy):
- "If two labels both apply, prefer the one that answers the prompt directly (choose primary). Annotate secondary as span note."
- "For truncated inputs (ellipsis or mid-sentence cut), mark with 'TRUNCATED' metadata and label conservatively."
- "If the example is a near-duplicate of another in the queue, check prior labels; if disagreement, flag for adjudication rather than relabeling."

Edge cases and decision heuristics (examples):
- Overlapping spans: prefer longer span unless the shorter span is strictly more specific (e.g., "San Francisco" vs "California" — pick finer-grain if task asks for city-level).
- Nested entities: mark both only if evaluation schema supports nested; otherwise, annotate the most task-relevant level.
- Ambiguous currency formats ("$100" vs "100 USD" vs "100$" in non-US locales): normalize to ISO currency in a metadata field rather than changing label.

Quick SQL/psuedo queries for stratification (examples):
- Rare-high-impact candidates:
  SELECT id FROM examples WHERE label_freq_30d < 0.005 AND (contains_pii = true OR safety_score > 0.7) LIMIT 200;
- Near-confusion sketch:
  SELECT id FROM predictions WHERE (top_score - second_score) < 0.08 ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 250;
- Duplication probe (using precomputed cluster_id):
  SELECT cluster_id, COUNT(*) as n, approx_entropy(labels) as ent FROM examples GROUP BY cluster_id HAVING n > 3 AND ent > 0.3 ORDER BY ent DESC LIMIT 50;

QA checks and quick metrics to compute after labeling pass:
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) by strata: Cohen's kappa for categorical, span IoU for entity tasks. Target: kappa>0.6 for frequent-clean, expect lower for near-confusion.
- Label flip rate vs history: percent of items whose label changed; investigate clusters with flip rate > 20%.
- False-positive surge detection: in rare-high-impact, check if model recall drops > 10% vs prior run.
- Time-per-example distribution to spot UI friction (expect median 18–35s depending on task complexity).

Adjudication rules (quick):
- If 2 labelers disagree and one marks 'abstain', send to adjudicator.
- For >3-way disagreement, escalate to specialist channel (#annotation-escalations) with 3 examples and short rationale.
- Use a lightweight adjudicator form: original text, labels chosen, brief comments, suggested final label.

UI/Tooling micro-ideas (fast wins):
- Show nearest-neighbor examples inline (collapsed) for duplication-probe to speed decisions.
- One-click 'mark as duplicate' that links to cluster id and auto-silences similar items for this batch.
- Quick metadata toggles ("TRUNCATED", "PII suspected") that set both the metadata flag and a free-text note area.

Examples (toy items) with desired outputs:
- "Invoice from ACME inc. total: $12,345.67" => label: FINANCIAL_RECORD; metadata: currency:USD; note: long_number_format.
- "Hey, drop by 7pm?" => label: PERSONAL_MESSAGE; metadata: none; edge: short casual.
- "[truncated] ... the code path returns NULL when" => label: BUG_REPORT_SNIPPET; metadata: TRUNCATED=true; action: escalate to dev-docs if unclear.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- What's a sensible threshold for (top - second) for multi-class tasks with >50 classes? (current 0.08 is empirical for 12–20 class problems). Need a sweep across tasks.
- Confirm interplay with caching: if example moved between runs due to rehashing, ensure training set dedupe still holds.
- Add an automated preflight that flags batches with >30% truncation/metadata-outliers to prevent wasted labeler time.

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Push prototype sampling script to label-tools (PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/label-tools/pull/78) and add unit tests for deterministic hashing. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Small litmus run: 500 examples using these strata next week; collect IAA and time-per-example. (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Draft short labeler microcopy and validate with two contractors before rolling to full pool. (owner: Evelyn)

Notes to self (short, informal):
- Keep quotas flexible; early runs will need manual nudges.
- Watch out for labeler fatigue in duplication-probe — rotate tasks.
- Consider a small 'challenge coin' bonus for labelers who find novel edge cases that lead to schema changes.

Slack / refs: #annotation, #annotation-escalations, JIRA LABEL-4321 (sampling design), LABEL-4489 (duplication dedupe).

-- A.P.
